target_customer: Addiction and mental health treatment programs and their directors
problem: Treatment programs lose time and revenue to documentation, utilization review paperwork and insurance denials, with staff shortages.
business_model: B2B SaaS and AI agents sold to behavioral health programs (pricing not public)
product_category: Behavioral health admin AI (chart audits, utilization review, scribe)

founders.name: Eshan Dosani
prior_employers: White House (drug policy work, per YC launch post)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page he spent about five years on addiction and mental health and ran a group doing overdose prevention work.

competitors.name: Eleos Health
competitors.what: AI documentation and quality tools for behavioral health
competitors.traction_then: A comparison page claims 200+ organizations and 40,000+ providers (vendor-sourced, undated)
competitors.funding_then: described as having raised more than peers; amount not verified

competitors.name: Upheal
competitors.what: AI note generation and session analytics for therapists

technical_complexity.rationale: LLM chart review against payer and documentation rules is standard applied AI, with HIPAA compliance and EHR data access as the harder parts.

defensibility.rationale: Many scribe vendors exist, and defensibility would come from payer rule data and workflow embedding, neither shown at founding.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or incumbent copy found.

market_need_then: The YC page and company site describe administrative burden, staff shortages and insurance denials. The company reports about $250K committed ARR within four weeks of launching Reclaim (self-reported).

identity.voice_and_tone: plain, compliance forward (HIPAA and BAA highlighted)

brand_strength.rationale: Generic health name on a .ai domain with no press on the brand found; product names Scribe and Reclaim collide with other companies.

outcome_analysis: Perspectives Health entered YC in Summer 2025 with a chart audit and utilization review product for addiction treatment programs. It reports early revenue and a dozen customer logos but no verified funding or exit, so its outcome is still open and the main risks are scribe competition and proving payer denial savings.
notes: An aggregator (VCBacked) lists $500K pre-seed in September 2025 from Y Combinator, unverified and not recorded as a round. Another source lists a different co-founder name that could not be confirmed. Competitor sources are undated vendor comparison pages, so competition as of founding is only approximate. Education and prior employers beyond the YC page not found. Audit fix: the $500K pre-seed (2025-09) is now recorded from VCBacked; Caplight shows the same total and adds IKJ Capital, so it rests on databases only, with no primary confirmation.
